tasks.question: On Windows, why does _rebuild_lock take its msvcrt lock on a byte far into the lock file instead of the first byte?

gold.statement: Windows byte-range locks are mandatory, so locking at offset 4096 lets external readers still read the owning PID written at byte 0 without getting a PermissionError.
The commit added msvcrt locking because the Windows fallback of yielding True left concurrent rebuilds unserialized, and they collided on .graph.tmp.json (closes #3881).

tasks.question: Why does res.clearCookie throw away any maxAge the caller passes and always overwrite expires with a date in the past, rather than respecting the options it was given?

gold.statement: Commit 82fc12a4 ("Ignore `expires` and `maxAge` in `res.clearCookie()` (#5792)", Jon Church, 2024-08-02) introduced the forced past expires and the deletion of maxAge.

Rationale: res.cookie turns maxAge into a relative expires, so a user-supplied maxAge (or expires) would overwrite the expiration that clearCookie needs. The goal is to stop users from accidentally overriding these values when clearing a cookie, without reworking the relative-expires behaviour of maxAge.
In 4.x this was first only deprecated: commit f42b160b (#5672) added a deprecation notice for res.clearCookie accepting options.maxAge/options.expires.

tasks.question: When toJSONObject converts an object, why does it take each object back out of its set of seen objects once it has finished walking that object's children, instead of leaving it marked as seen for the rest of the conversion?

gold.statement: Removing the object after its children are processed keeps the check limited to the current path (ancestors only). Only a real cycle, meaning an object that contains itself somewhere below it, is skipped.
Without the removal, an object shared by two siblings (a DAG) would be treated as already seen at its second occurrence and dropped as undefined. That is the regression introduced in #7230.
The WeakSet replaced a fixed-size Array(10) with an indexOf lookup. Faster O(1) lookups were a secondary benefit (#10832, fixes #10807).

tasks.question: In the Unix terminal renderer's cancellable key-read path, why does an interrupted select() call loop forever instead of counting toward a retry limit?

gold.statement: Counting EINTR against the 100-iteration limit (meant for read attempts, reset only when a byte was read) let signals during an idle prompt drain it; running out returned getCharError, which became a Fatal event and exit status 2.
Only the cancellable path (used with --listen) is affected, because select() is not restarted by SA_RESTART, unlike the blocking read on the non-cancellable path.
The fix matches waitReadable(), which already retries EINTR without a limit; it fixes issue #4917.

tasks.question: In the router tree's case-insensitive path lookup, why does the code try a node's static children first and only then take the wildcard child from the end of the children list, rather than just taking the first child?

gold.statement: With RedirectFixedPath enabled, a request that matched no route made findCaseInsensitivePathRec panic with "invalid node type". The code took children[0] as the wildcard child, but addChild() keeps the wildcard child at the end of the array. So when a node had both static and wildcard children, children[0] was a static node and the switch on nType fell through to the default panic. The fix does what getValue() already did and uses children[len(children)-1] for the wildcard child (Fixes #2959).

Static children are tried first, through indices, before the wildcard child. This was added after review so that static routes beat param routes in case-insensitive matching: /PREFIX/XXX should resolve to /prefix/xxx and not match :id.

tasks.question: If I changed filterFlags so that it no longer cuts a header value at the first space or semicolon, what code would behave differently or need updating?

gold.statement: filterFlags returns the part of the string before the first ' ' or ';', or the whole string if neither is present. It was introduced in 9634a38 (2014-07-04) for the new JSON/XML/form binding code. In dc43372 (2014-07-16) it moved into utils.go when the source was split into files.

Its only production caller is Context.ContentType, which returns filterFlags(c.requestHeader("Content-Type")). With the change, ContentType would return the full header including parameters such as '; charset=utf-8'.
Context.Bind passes c.ContentType() to binding.Default to choose the binding. Bind would then pick a different binding for requests whose Content-Type has parameters.
Context.ShouldBind also passes c.ContentType() to binding.Default, so it is affected in the same way.

binding.Default switches on exact MIME constants such as MIMEJSON and MIMEXML, and its default branch returns Form. An unfiltered value like 'application/json; charset=utf-8' would match no case and fall through to form binding.
The gin.Bind middleware wrapper calls c.Bind(obj), so it is affected through Context.Bind.
TestFilterFlags checks the helper directly: 'text/html ' and 'text/html;' must both give 'text/html'.
TestContextContentType sets 'application/json; charset=utf-8' and expects ContentType() to return 'application/json'. It would break.

tasks.question: If I changed the parameters or return type of Idn::convertUri, which code in the library and its tests would have to be updated?

gold.statement: The client calls Idn::convertUri when it builds the request URI, if IDN conversion is enabled.
The redirect middleware calls Idn::convertUri on the redirect target URI.

The ProxyEnv unit tests call resolveProxySelection directly.
